enhanced.fullText:
The Emergency Planning and Community Right to Know Act (EPCRA), codified at 42 U.S.C. §§ 11001-11050, establishes comprehensive emergency planning and hazardous substance reporting requirements that significantly impact higher education institutions. This federal legislation, also known as Title III of the Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act (SARA), creates a framework for community emergency planning and requires facilities to report on their storage, use, and releases of hazardous substances.

Under 42 U.S.C. § 11001, EPCRA mandates the establishment of State Emergency Response Commissions (SERCs) and Tribal Emergency Response Commissions (TERCs), which coordinate emergency response activities and appoint Local Emergency Planning Committees (LEPCs). Higher education institutions must engage with these entities when they meet threshold requirements for hazardous substance storage or usage.

Section 302 (42 U.S.C. § 11002) requires facilities that store extremely hazardous substances (EHS) at or above threshold planning quantities to notify their SERC and LEPC. Universities operating research laboratories, physical plant operations, or health facilities often trigger these requirements through chemical storage for academic and operational purposes. The EPA maintains a list of over 350 EHS substances with specific threshold quantities ranging from 1 to 10,000 pounds.

Section 303 (42 U.S.C. § 11003) mandates that facilities provide emergency planning information to LEPCs, including facility emergency coordinators, chemical inventory data, and emergency response procedures. Universities must designate qualified personnel to serve as emergency contacts and coordinate with local emergency planners.

The reporting provisions under Sections 311-312 (42 U.S.C. §§ 11021-11022) require facilities to submit Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) or Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and annual chemical inventory reports (Tier I/II forms) for hazardous chemicals stored above threshold quantities. Universities typically must report chemicals used in research laboratories, maintenance operations, and campus utilities.

Section 313 (42 U.S.C. § 11023) establishes the Toxic Release Inventory (TRI) program, requiring annual reporting of toxic chemical releases and waste management activities. While fewer universities trigger TRI reporting requirements, those with significant research operations, power plants, or manufacturing activities may be subject to these provisions.

Implementation is governed by 40 CFR Parts 355, 370, and 372, which specify reporting forms, deadlines, and threshold quantities. The EPA enforces EPCRA provisions and may impose civil penalties up to $27,500 per day per violation under 42 U.S.C. § 11045. State and local authorities may also enforce certain provisions.

EPCRA's public disclosure provisions ensure that all submitted information becomes publicly accessible unless protected by valid trade secret claims under 42 U.S.C. § 11042. This transparency requirement means university chemical inventories and emergency planning information are available to community members, creating accountability for campus safety practices.

Recent amendments have increased penalty amounts and expanded covered chemicals. Universities must regularly review their chemical inventories against updated EHS lists and threshold quantities to ensure continued compliance with evolving requirements.
enhanced.summary: EPCRA requires higher education institutions storing hazardous chemicals above threshold quantities to report to emergency planning committees, submit annual chemical inventories, and coordinate emergency response planning with local authorities.
enhanced.requirements:
## Emergency Planning Coordination
- Notify SERC and LEPC within 60 days when storing extremely hazardous substances above threshold planning quantities
- Designate facility emergency coordinator for liaison with local emergency planners
- Provide emergency response procedures and facility layout information to LEPC

## Chemical Inventory Reporting
- Submit MSDS/SDS for all hazardous chemicals stored above 10,000 pounds or threshold planning quantities
- File annual Tier II inventory reports by March 1st detailing chemical storage amounts and locations
- Maintain current chemical inventory records for regulatory access

## Toxic Release Inventory (TRI)
- File Form R reports by July 1st for covered toxic chemicals processed or used above threshold quantities
- Report releases to air, water, and land from university operations
- Document waste management and pollution prevention activities

## Public Information Management
- Ensure submitted information accuracy as reports become publicly accessible
- Evaluate trade secret protection claims for proprietary research chemicals
- Coordinate with legal counsel on information disclosure implications
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Annual Tier II chemical inventory reports due March 1st to SERC, LEPC, and local fire department. TRI Form R reports due July 1st to EPA and state agencies. Emergency notification required within 60 days of exceeding EHS threshold quantities. Immediate release reporting required for reportable quantity spills.
